Πῠᾰνόψια (sc. ἱερά), τά, an Athenian festival in the month Πυανοψιών, in honour of Apollo, Lycurg. Fr. 84 : elsewh. written Πυανέψια (cf. sq.) and expld. fr. πύανον ἕψειν, of a dish of beans cooked and offered,
Plu. Thes. 22 , Ath. 10.408a , etc.; acc. to Lycurg.l.c. the other Greeks called it Πανόψια ( Πανοψίαν codd.).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
